title: Add Graceful Shutdown with In‑Flight Request Tracking
description: Implements a production‑ready graceful shutdown mechanism that listens for SIGINT/SIGTERM, stops accepting new connections, waits for ongoing requests to finish (with a configurable timeout), and logs shutdown progress. This reduces abrupt terminations and improves reliability in containerized environments.
testCases: Simulate SIGTERM while a long‑running request is in flight and verify the server stops accepting new requests but completes the existing one before exiting
Trigger shutdown with no active requests and ensure the process exits immediately after cleanup callbacks run
acceptance: When a termination signal is received, the server must stop accepting new connections, allow active requests to finish within the timeout (default 10 s), log each shutdown step, and exit with code 0. If the timeout expires, pending requests are aborted and the process exits with code 1. All unit and integration tests pass.
reason: Ensures yantraverse can be safely deployed in production orchestration platforms (Kubernetes, Docker Swarm) where graceful termination is required to avoid dropped requests and improve overall service stability.
